key_insight: A recurrent neural network trained for free recall can learn multiple, human-like memory strategies—not just one classical temporal-context mechanism. The best-performing models often use an index-based strategy that resembles the memory palace technique.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the question of how AI models can explain and reproduce human free recall behavior, especially whether a single temporal-context model is sufficient to capture the diversity of memory strategies people use.
method: Train recurrent neural networks on free recall tasks and optimize them to match human recall performance.
Compare the learned internal strategies against classical memory models, especially temporal context approaches.
Analyze the best-performing networks to identify whether they rely on temporal context, indexing, or hybrid memory mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that end-to-end training on cognitive tasks can uncover richer internal algorithms than hand-designed assumptions. It also suggests new architectures for memory-intensive systems that use multiple retrieval strategies instead of a single fixed mechanism.

paper_title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
paper_authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar
